compareCandidate.label: Percent vs. fraction
compareCandidate.description: A percent is a special fraction with a fixed denominator of 100 — 25% is always 25/100. A fraction can have any denominator. Percents make comparisons uniform: 25% and 40% are instantly comparable.

processes: Converting percent to fraction and decimal
plainLanguageExplanation: Percent means 'per hundred' or 'out of 100'. If you score 25% on a 100-mark test, you got 25 marks. The 'percent grid' shows this perfectly: a 10-by-10 grid of 100 squares, and every shaded square is one percent. 50% means half the grid lit. Percent, fraction, and decimal are just three spellings of the same idea: 25% = 25/100 = 0.25. To find a percent of a number, you can convert to a decimal and multiply — 50% of 200 is 0.5 × 200 = 100. Sales ('30% off'), scores, and statistics all use percents because the 'out of 100' scale makes different situations easy to compare.

keyFacts.label: Grid
keyFacts.value: Each square of a 10×10 grid is 1%

whyItMatters: Percents appear everywhere — discounts, test scores, interest, statistics, nutrition labels. Understanding percent as 'out of 100' lets you quickly compute discounts, understand data, and make sense of the numbers plastered across daily life.
didYouKnow: The % symbol evolved from the Latin 'per centum'. Merchants wrote 'per 100' so often they abbreviated it — eventually the letters mashed together into the % sign you see today.
compareReason: Percent and decimal are two spellings of the same 'out of a hundred' idea — comparing 25% with 0.25 ties them together forever.
